children: Physicswallah shares jumped 6 percent in late-morning trade on September 4 after Motilal Oswal initiated coverage on the edtech company with a 'Buy' rating and a target price of Rs 200, implying an upside of about 66 percent from the previous close.

The stock was trading around Rs 127.8, among the top gainers on both BSE 500 and NSE 500 indices. Today’s rise took Physicswallah's market capitalisation to about Rs 36,777 crore. The shares have declined 4.5 percent so far in 2026, compared with an 8.3 percent fall in the Nifty 50.

Motilal Oswal cited Physicswallah's low customer-acquisition costs, scalable online business and the long runway for digital penetration in India's education market. The brokerage said the company's large YouTube presence has created a free-to-paid funnel that allows it to acquire students at structurally lower costs and monetise them across online, hybrid and offline offerings.
Physicswallah has more than 100 million YouTube subscribers and its revenue has compounded at around 74 percent annually between FY23 and FY26, according to the brokerage.

Motilal Oswal sees the online business as the company's primary value driver and expects its revenue to grow at around 28 percent CAGR over FY26-30, supported by paid-user growth, category expansion and AI-led monetisation. It expects pre-Ind AS EBITDA margins to improve from around 26 percent in FY26 to 30 percent by FY28.

The brokerage also sees considerable room for digital adoption. Online penetration in flagship JEE and NEET categories is around 20 percent. On the other hand, penetration in newer segments such as foundation courses, state boards and government examinations remains below 1 percent.

Physicswallah's offline business, which expanded from 28 centres in FY23 to 353 by FY26-end, is expected to grow at around 20 percent CAGR over FY26-30. Motilal Oswal believes the aggressive expansion phase is nearing its end, which should help improve utilisation and profitability as newer centres mature.

The brokerage valued Physicswallah on a sum-of-the-parts basis, assigning 50 times FY28 estimated EV/EBITDA to the online business and 15 times to the offline business. After adjusting for cash, it arrived at a target price of Rs 200. Key risks include greater competition, weak offline execution, faculty attrition and adverse regulatory changes.

Separately, around 41.4 lakh Physicswallah shares changed hands through the block deal window in morning trade on Friday. Details of the buyers, sellers and transaction price were not immediately available. At Thursday's closing price of Rs 120.6, the shares would be worth just under Rs 50 crore.

The trade comes a little over a week after Lightspeed Venture Partners exited Physicswallah by selling its entire 1.61 percent stake. Lightspeed Opportunity Fund II LP sold 4.67 crore shares for Rs 549.73 crore on August 26 at Rs 117.72 apiece.

The shares were picked up by several global and domestic institutional investors. ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund was the largest buyer, acquiring a 0.75 percent stake for Rs 258.98 crore, while Goldman Sachs bought around 0.3 percent for Rs 105.56 crore. Other buyers included Morgan Stanley Asia Singapore, Societe Generale, Citigroup Global Markets Mauritius and Tata AIA Life Insurance Company.
